# Test audit

- [x] Isolate the committed baseline on test-audit.
- [x] Run baseline Vitest, Docker, and CI scenarios.
- [x] Inventory features independently and review every original test file.
- [x] Complete all original test actions.
- [x] Reconcile surviving faults and every changed/new test kill.
- [x] Complete the feature protection matrix and fill unprotected feature gaps.
- [x] Run final checks and verify only explicitly accepted application repairs.

The baseline was green, but 732 of 1748 source test declarations failed the behavior standard in the reviewed classification ledger. The original test audit at ec1955434bbd43136d8bbf3b92ef8d696aa78a38 changed no application code. The current repair review records 7 fixed, 7 open and 1 deferred defects. Approved application repairs and current case evidence are recorded in [test-audit/adversarial/acceptance.json](test-audit/adversarial/acceptance.json). The latest full suite passes 1746 runtime cases, including 27 documented expected failures, with 0 unexpected failures and 0 skipped tests. All test actions and mutation proofs are reconciled. The feature matrix identifies 21 obligations with no Strong test protection. See [test-audit/ledger.json](test-audit/ledger.json) and [test-audit/adversarial/repair-unit-full.json](test-audit/adversarial/repair-unit-full.json).

## Counts before and after

| Classification | Before source declarations | After source declarations |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| STRONG | 1016 | 1568 |
| WEAK | 296 | 0 |
| HOLLOW | 47 | 0 |
| COUPLED | 338 | 0 |
| DEAD | 1 | 0 |
| MISLABELED | 50 | 0 |

The baseline contains 1748 source declarations in 296 TypeScript files, expanded by Vitest into 1802 runtime cases. The current inventory contains 1568 source declarations in 214 files. Deletions and many-to-one rewrites are counted separately in [test-audit/ledger.json](test-audit/ledger.json); deleted tests are not counted as DEAD tests. Eight shell/CI logical cases are reported separately below.

The baseline passed 1801 tests, with 1 skipped and zero failures, in 109.83 seconds. Docker passed six cases in 11.12 seconds. The original inline CI scenarios passed despite incomplete search assertions. The latest full suite passed 1746 tests, including 27 expected-failure regressions, with 0 unexpected failures and 0 skipped, in 109.49 seconds. See [test-audit/evidence/baseline.json](test-audit/evidence/baseline.json) and [test-audit/adversarial/repair-unit-full.json](test-audit/adversarial/repair-unit-full.json). Source classifications and changed declarations are independently joined to runtime evidence in [test-audit/reconciliation.json](test-audit/reconciliation.json).

## Defects found

### D-G3-001: Exported fnv1a does not compute the documented 32-bit FNV-1a hash

Independently reproduced in the root audit worktree. BigInt XOR/multiply/modulo-2^32 arithmetic gives 4f9f2cab; the exported function returns a82fb4a1. Its floating-point multiplication loses low bits.

Expected: 4f9f2cab

Originally observed: a82fb4a1

Current resolution: deferred. DEFERRED at the user's direction. The ordinary FNV regression still fails; no hash repair was incorporated.

Current reproduction: `node scripts/test-audit-reproduce-current.mjs D-G3-001`. Retained as an expected failure; ordinary failure evidence establishes the unresolved defect.

Current evidence: [test-audit/adversarial/final-open-ordinary.json](test-audit/adversarial/final-open-ordinary.json).

Historical evidence: [test-audit/evidence/group3-hash-defect.json](test-audit/evidence/group3-hash-defect.json), [test-audit/evidence/D-G3-001.reproduced.json](test-audit/evidence/D-G3-001.reproduced.json), [test-audit/mutations/hash.repair.results.json](test-audit/mutations/hash.repair.results.json).

### D-VSC-001: VS Code reinforcement omits the required signal and supplies a file path as a memory ID

The public extension command was invoked through a VS Code host boundary double and executed the local CLI. A temporary probe supplying --signal useful and the fixture memory ID makes the expected-failure test unexpectedly pass.

Expected: The selected memory receives useful reinforcement and its persisted modified date becomes today.

Originally observed: The real CLI rejects the command because --signal is required; the memory remains dated 2000-01-01.

Current resolution: open. OPEN. The selected ID and useful signal are still missing. Corrected QA fixtures supply real document text and no longer require launching for unreadable IDs. This also blocks positive nested-path and hostile-filename reinforcement cases.

Current reproduction: `node scripts/test-audit-reproduce-current.mjs D-VSC-001`. Retained as an expected failure; ordinary failure evidence establishes the unresolved defect.

Current evidence: [test-audit/adversarial/final-open-ordinary.json](test-audit/adversarial/final-open-ordinary.json).

Historical evidence: [test-audit/evidence/vscode-defect-reproduction.json](test-audit/evidence/vscode-defect-reproduction.json), [test-audit/mutations/vscode.repairs.results.json](test-audit/mutations/vscode.repairs.results.json), [test-audit/evidence/D-VSC-001.reproduced.json](test-audit/evidence/D-VSC-001.reproduced.json).

### D-VSC-002: VS Code memory-directory validation accepts names such as .gnosys-other

The selected path ends in .gnosys-other/memory.md. Requiring an exact path component makes the expected-failure test unexpectedly pass.

Expected: The outside-memory-directory warning appears and reinforcement is not invoked.

Originally observed: Substring validation accepts .gnosys-other and invokes the reinforcement subprocess.

Current resolution: fixed. Ordinary passing cases and direct fault replays verify the accepted repair.

### D-VSC-003: VS Code reinforcement evaluates shell syntax in selected filenames

The real shell ran only a harmless touch command inside the temporary test project. Replacing shell interpolation with execFileSync argument passing makes the expected-failure test unexpectedly pass.

Expected: The literal argument decisions/$(touch audit-injected).md reaches the CLI without evaluating the shell expression.

Originally observed: The argument becomes decisions/.md and a harmless audit-injected marker is created in the isolated fixture directory.

Current resolution: open. OPEN, partially repaired. Reinforcement uses shell-free argv, but the dashboard still invokes a shell through terminal.sendText. The user's extension-wide requirement fails. The CLI accepts a memory ID, so filename cases now require reading that literal selected file and passing its real ID.

Current reproduction: `node scripts/test-audit-reproduce-current.mjs D-VSC-003`. Retained as an expected failure; ordinary failure evidence establishes the unresolved defect.

Current evidence: [test-audit/adversarial/final-open-ordinary.json](test-audit/adversarial/final-open-ordinary.json).

Historical evidence: [test-audit/evidence/vscode-defect-reproduction.json](test-audit/evidence/vscode-defect-reproduction.json), [test-audit/mutations/vscode.repairs.results.json](test-audit/mutations/vscode.repairs.results.json), [test-audit/evidence/D-VSC-003.reproduced.json](test-audit/evidence/D-VSC-003.reproduced.json).

The real summary wizard receives 2,4,y,done and its project config is reloaded. updateConfig recursively merges the empty taskModels object, retaining previous keys. A temporary clear-overrides repair makes the expected-failure test unexpectedly pass.

Current resolution: open. OPEN. Reset retains task overrides. Four ordinary wizard regressions fail, including the corrected all-ollama summary. Unrelated serialized config values remain unchanged; v584 tests remain byte-identical.

Originally observed: The cancellation message appears but the process exits0.

Current resolution: fixed. Ordinary passing cases and direct fault replays verify the accepted repair.

## Feature protection matrix

The inventory was derived from README, documentation, CLI/MCP registration, and exported modules before reading tests. Its 41 feature groups have 164 success, failure, boundary, and permission obligations. A passing expected-failure regression detects a known defect; it does not establish correct application behavior. Help contracts protect registration and documentation only. See [test-audit/features.json](test-audit/features.json) for source references.

The initial F37 inventory incorrectly attributed socket-server read/update operations to the generated helper. Documentation and public exports establish its actual API. The original inventory and exact correction are preserved in [test-audit/features.original.json](test-audit/features.original.json) and [test-audit/inventory-corrections.json](test-audit/inventory-corrections.json). Final mapping corrections are recorded in [test-audit/feature-map-corrections.json](test-audit/feature-map-corrections.json).

0 whole feature groups have no passing Strong behavior test. 21 individual obligations have no mapped Strong behavior test. PARTIAL means only the stated subset is protected; the Limits column records the remaining gaps. KNOWN_DEFECT means an ordinary reproduction contradicts the contract. Platform blocks are explicit. These statuses describe protection for the stated obligation, not line coverage.

## Mutation results

The selected post-repair fault set killed 505/508 distinct mutations (99.41%). This is a targeted manual score, not a full-program or random mutation score. Original-test experiments and inverse repair probes for known defects are excluded. A mutation that causes only a build or harness failure does not count as killed. Repeated copies of evidence are deduplicated in [test-audit/ledger.json](test-audit/ledger.json).

The score retains three surviving draft experiments. G1-lens-author and G1-lens-authority rotated fixture indexes by two, which returned the already-correct records for those selections. Rotating by one in the corrected faults produces wrong records and is killed by the final tests. The g2-dream-closed-db draft did not reach the injected error branch and was discarded; retained scheduling cases have separate killed faults. These survivors are visible in the table and do not count as proof for a rewritten test.

The mutation runner restores exact original application bytes after each experiment, verifies the application digest, and reruns the selected tests. Fixed defects require ordinary passing cases and direct fault-injection pass/fail/pass evidence on the accepted application. Open and deferred expected failures require an ordinary failing reproduction; no temporary repair is required. These probes do not establish successful feature behavior.

## Repeated patterns

- Source-string checks accepted broken command placement and skipped writes. The replacement CLI contracts check literal command paths; handler behavior is covered separately.
- Type, existence, and broad count assertions accepted wrong records, truncated artifacts, and wrong metadata. Replacements assert literal results and persisted content.
- Fixture-only tests and tests that manually performed both writes did not exercise the advertised workflow. Duplicates were deleted with named replacement coverage.
- Application mocks bypassed the logic under test. Replacements use real application modules and confine doubles to external boundaries such as network, OS commands, terminal input, and the model runtime.
- Conditional assertions and empty loops accepted missing outputs. Replacements assert the expected result set before inspecting its contents.
- The CI search-isolation results were printed without assertions. The renamed local-storage scenario never mounted a network share; its test now claims only the local behavior it exercises.

## Scope, verification, and blockers

This audit targets the committed gnosys-public package at 203c4e7e488cea66bfd9a3ad687d9d1dda309d16 (6.2.1), in an isolated test-audit worktree. The workspace root is not a repository. The original checkout has unrelated uncommitted changes and remains outside this audit. No push or PR is authorized.

The original completed audit remains at ec1955434bbd43136d8bbf3b92ef8d696aa78a38. Current application bytes and executable modes must match f4b9135ae350fad937a66f03a9bc3ccfbd8c6906; replaying only the approved application-fix commits from that audit commit must produce the same application tree. Extra application edits remain rejected. Approved commits: b8ac52bb1f18e6977fc45c1914e07610888cf652, 13756f2c1aab1873ba7d68a39727b16b11251a29, e2c08a37e7c69745e1dd4effc1bbe97f6e01b8b7, 636e03271db7ee670374c846cff747ecd0318d85, 3021bf5c88d5ec11ab3b61f311a68ba5c15a7f07, a420e3b727c33a578aed2c089d72841f5a4441f9, 29a59b0b8ecdeb6e0796515d787aada530fe7335, 6a69746dabf618e212c23e5530b474903d19df07, f4b9135ae350fad937a66f03a9bc3ccfbd8c6906.

Node 22.17.1, Vitest 4.1.9, TypeScript 5.9.3, tsx 4.22.4, better-sqlite3 11.10.0, and MCP SDK 1.29.0 match the installed baseline dependencies. CI collects src/**/*.test.ts on Linux and macOS; runner exclusions cover dist and node_modules. Coverage exclusions are distinct from test collection and are not evidence of protection. Docker setup and the two CI scenarios run in separate jobs. The npm test, coverage, and watch commands now build before starting, so CLI subprocess tests begin with current compiled artifacts.

The sandbox initially rejected loopback listeners with EPERM. Authorized local HTTP/PTY runs pass. Docker setup tests run without networking or host mounts. Real provider credentials, operating-system integration, and physical network-share behavior are reported as unverified where boundary doubles or temporary local directories are used.

- Adversarial review: seven fixed, seven open and one deferred defect at application revision f4b9135. All requested attacks and limitations are listed in [repair review](test-audit/adversarial/REVIEW.md).
- Full suite: 1,746 passed, zero unexpected failures or skipped cases, including 27 documented expected failures; 109.49 seconds. Evidence: [full suite](test-audit/adversarial/repair-unit-full.json).
- Coverage suite: 1,746 passed in 118.04 seconds; configured thresholds passed. Statements 71.64%, branches 61.39%, functions 81.18%, lines 73.57%. Evidence: [coverage run](test-audit/adversarial/final-coverage-suite.json) and [summary](test-audit/adversarial/final-coverage-summary.json).
- Typecheck, lint and npm run knip exit 0. Lint retains 23 warnings. Both real CLI CI scenarios pass. Evidence: [static and CI checks](test-audit/adversarial/final-static-ci-checks.json).
- All six setup Docker scenarios pass against the packed CLI using ephemeral tmpfs fixture directories, without network or host mounts. The default run hit a full Docker overlay before four fixture directories could be created; both receipts are preserved. Evidence: [tmpfs replay](test-audit/adversarial/final-docker-tmpfs.json) and [default run](test-audit/adversarial/final-docker-setup.json).
- The new-file coverage guard exits 2 for an unresolved base and 0 against the pinned baseline. The renamed local-storage workflow makes no network-share claim. Direct CI faults are killed. Evidence: [checks](test-audit/adversarial/final-static-ci-checks.json), [CI review](test-audit/adversarial/ci-review.json), [CI fault proofs](test-audit/adversarial/ci-http.results.json).
- All 1,748 original declarations, 1,568 current declarations and 1,746 runtime cases reconcile with zero action, classification, source-body or mutation-proof gaps. Every original WEAK/HOLLOW rating retains surviving-fault evidence or an explicit structural reason. Evidence: [ledger](test-audit/ledger.json) and [reconciliation](test-audit/reconciliation.json).
- Seven fixed defects have ordinary passing cases and current direct fault pass/fail/pass proofs. All 27 remaining expected-failure runtime cases fail as ordinary tests. D-G3-001 stays DEFERRED. Inverse repair unexpected passes receive no successful protection credit. Evidence: [acceptance](test-audit/adversarial/acceptance.json) and [ordinary failures](test-audit/adversarial/final-open-ordinary.json).
- All ten original KNOWN_DEFECT matrix rows were restated from current evidence; the inventory remains 41 feature groups and 164 obligations. Evidence: [row-by-row restatus](test-audit/adversarial/feature-restatus.json).
- Application bytes and modes match the frozen repair revision. Replaying only the nine listed application commits from completed audit ec19554 produces the same application tree; later application work is excluded. Evidence: [source integrity](test-audit/adversarial/final-source-integrity.json).
- The v584 updateConfig and 50/100 ms read-test files remain byte-identical to the completed audit revision and pass. Evidence: [unchanged files](test-audit/adversarial/unchanged-compatibility-tests.json).
- The report acceptance validator passes 24 controlled checks, including rejection of stale runtime data, unlisted application edits, inverse-only repair evidence and expected failures claimed as successful protection. Metadata generators produce identical output on replay. Evidence: [validator](test-audit/adversarial/report-validation.results.json) and [metadata replay](test-audit/adversarial/metadata-replay.json).
- Behavior-over-implementation changed the VS Code fixtures to require the selected document ID and useful signal, and corrected the routing summary to expect cleared overrides. Build-the-lever produced reusable ordinary-defect reproduction, reconciliation and matrix update scripts.
- First CI run watchlist: src/test/phase7b.read-paths.test.ts:104 requires reading 100 memories in under 100 ms; line124 requires FTS search in under 50 ms. Hosted-runner contention, scheduling and cold caches may exceed these wall-clock limits. Both assertions remain unchanged.
- The default Docker run encountered a 100%-full overlay filesystem (0 bytes available, inodes48% used). Four scenarios failed while creating fixture directories. The same image and unchanged six tests passed with ephemeral tmpfs fixture directories. No Docker data was deleted; the normal local Docker runner remains capacity-limited.
- Live provider credentials/services, native keychain and scheduler integration, a running VS Code extension host, native Windows path handling and physical network-share behavior were not exercised. Tests use local HTTP boundaries, host doubles, real subprocesses and isolated temporary storage. The feature matrix names these limits.
- Verification used local macOS Node22.17.1 and the isolated Node22 Docker image. Other configured remote CI matrix combinations were not run; no push or PR was authorized.
- The unresolved-base behavior is fixed. The coverage guard still skips added files absent from its coverage summary; the pinned-base pass adds no application modules and does not establish coverage for excluded modules. The original COLL-03 record is historical evidence; this is its remaining limit.
